text:
Step–by–step analysis

1. Starting material  
(R)-(+)-Limonene is 1-methyl-4-(1-methylethenyl)-cyclohex-1-ene.  
• It contains two C=C double bonds:  
  – one endocyclic (between C-1 and C-2 of the ring)  
  – one exocyclic (the isopropenyl group at C-4).  
• It possesses one stereogenic centre at C-4, having the R-configuration.

2. Hydrogenation (Pd/C, 1 equiv H₂)  
The more accessible exocyclic C=C is reduced first.  
CH₂=C(Me)– (isopropenyl) → CH₃–CH(Me)– (isopropyl)  
The internal ring double bond remains; the configuration at C-4 (R) is unchanged.  
Product 1: 4-isopropyl-1-methylcyclohex-1-ene (4R).

3. Epoxidation with m-CPBA  
Peracids add to alkenes by a syn mechanism, giving the 1,2-epoxide.  
We obtain mainly one diastereomeric epoxide because the existing 4R centre biases attack from the less-hindered face.

4. Epoxide opening with NaOMe  
Under basic conditions MeO⁻ attacks the LESS-substituted carbon of the epoxide from the backside, giving trans ring-opening:  
C-2 receives OMe (with inversion), the epoxide oxygen remains on C-1 as an alkoxide → after protonation gives 1-OH and 2-OMe trans to each other.  
Thus C-1 and C-2 become new stereocentres of opposite configuration (one R, one S).

5. Esterification (propanoic acid, DCC, DMAP)  
Only the hydroxyl at C-1 is acylated, giving the propionate ester; the methoxy on C-2 is unchanged.

6. Stereochemistry in the major isomer  
• C-4 keeps its original R configuration.  
• C-1 and C-2 are trans; therefore their absolute configurations are opposite.  
The major diastereomer from step 3 has O (later propionyloxy) and CH₃ at C-1 on the same face as the original limonene methyl (to minimise A¹,³-strain), giving C-1 the S configuration, while C-2 (bearing OMe) is R.

Putting this together gives:  
(1S,2R,4R)-4-isopropyl-2-methoxy-1-methylcyclohexyl propionate.

Among the options, this corresponds to choice (A).

Answer: A
